transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, thanks, Doctor. Um… I guess what brought me in is people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said, so I have to ask them to repeat it. I don’t mean to be rude or anything… it just keeps happening enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Do you often feel excessively sleepy or drowsy during the day, even after what seems like a full night's sleep?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like I’m nodding off during the day or anything. I mean, I get tired like anybody after work, but I wouldn’t say I’m excessively sleepy after a full night’s sleep. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty paying attention or tuning things out since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid or anything, but it was definitely there back then too. Teachers moved my seat around a lot because I couldn’t really stay put, and I’d call out answers before I was supposed to. I remember getting in trouble for butting into other kids’ work too, even before middle school. So… yeah, not just recently, I guess.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have bad moods like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or stopped enjoying things lately. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, longstanding difficulty sustaining attention (missing parts of conversations, needing repetition) combined with childhood history of hyperactive-impulsive behaviors (couldn't stay seated, blurted answers, interrupted others). Symptoms began before age 12 and persist into adulthood, causing functional impairment in work and marital relationships. No evidence of excessive daytime sleepiness, depressive episode, or other mood/psychotic symptoms that would better explain the presentation, supporting a diagnosis of combined-type ADHD.
